subject: Evidence transfer and retention procedure after incident
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: preservation + export of logs after incident

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick responses over the phone this morning. We have a forensic request coming from our internal responders and counsel. High-level asks:

- Can Redwood preserve and export all relevant logs for our tenant (Acme Corp) covering 2027-04-27 00:00:00 UTC through 2027-04-29 23:59:59 UTC? We need audit logs, request/response traces, and any system-level logs relating to auth events and key operations.
- Please confirm where those logs are stored (region/zone) and whether they contain any customer PII by default.
- We will need a chain-of-custody statement and an immutable export for our external forensics partner (BlueSky Forensics). What format and transfer methods do you support?
- Finally, after we agree on evidence transfer, what is Redwood's standard window for retaining these exported copies, and what are the steps to request deletion once our investigation is complete?

We can sign an evidence transfer addendum if required. Please let me know the ETA for an initial preservation action (e.g., disabling auto-deletes) and a timeline for a full export.

Thanks,
Tom Alvarez
Head of Security Operations
Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com

--
Note: we may need signed authorization from Acme legal before some exports; happy to coordinate guidance on that if helpful.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: preservation + export of logs after incident

Tom -- thanks for the clear list. We can start preservation immediately and outline the export options. Quick answers up front:

- Preservation action: we will create an immutable snapshot of audit and request logs for the specified window and suspend any auto-deletion/compaction for the tenant. ETA: preservation step started within 2 hours; confirmation when snapshot is complete.
- Location/residency: your tenant data is hosted in us-east-1 for the affected resources. Exports will remain in that region unless you request cross-region transfer.
- PII: request-level logs may include user identifiers and request payloads depending on your settings. We will not redact anything in the immutable export unless you instruct us to do so; we will provide a redaction/filtered export option if required.
- Chain-of-custody & transfer: we can produce an export bundle (gzip) plus a signed chain_of_custody text file and provide an S3 pre-signed URL or a secure Drive link (we typically use an encrypted workspace with BlueSky Forensics).
- Retention after export: standard practice is to hold the exported bundle for 90 days by default unless you request earlier deletion in writing. We can extend this on request.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please confirm that Acme legal authorizes the export and whether you want unredacted logs.
2) I'll loop in our forensics ops lead (Rishi) and incident ops (Stephanie) to coordinate the export job and COC documentation.
3) We will provide an initial export manifest (sample attached) and an ETA for the full export (typically 48-72 hours).

Attachment: audit-log-export-20270429.csv (sample manifest with filenames and checksums).

I'll follow up shortly with internal coordination notes.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Please confirm any blockers. Stephanie, can you coordinate the external contact for BlueSky and confirm whether we need a signed evidence-transfer addendum before transfer? Rishi, please confirm that the export will include request payloads unredacted by default and outline the PII redaction options.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 06:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: ACME export runbook + preservation actions (CONFIDENTIAL)

Confirmed. Technical notes / constraints:

- Log locations: audit logs are stored in s3://redwood-logs-us-east-1/audit/acct-ACME-0047/, request traces in s3://redwood-traces-us-east-1/requests/acct-ACME-0047/, and cache snapshots in kv-archive/us-east-1/acct-ACME-0047/.
- Exports: we can produce a full unredacted export that includes request bodies and headers. Because request bodies may contain PII, we require written authorization from the data controller (Acme) to transfer unredacted content. If we receive only an operational request, we will provide redacted exports by default (redaction removes declared PII fields and token-level content).
- Timeline & capacity: export jobs for a single tenant typically take 24-72 hours depending on size; ballpark for this tenant is ~36 hours. We will throttle to avoid impacting live production.
- KMS: using cmk-acme-01 to wrap the final bundle; we will not export unwrapped secrets.
- Chain of custody: operator will compute SHA256 checksums for each file and include operator principal names and timestamps; file notes will be recorded in chain_of_custody_20270504.txt.
- Deletion: we can mark the exported bundle for 90-day retention and will delete on a documented written request. Deletion of original snapshots will follow the incident retention policy only after approval from security/legal.

I will kick off the export after Stephanie confirms BlueSky contact and Acme authorization. Attaching the internal manifest for traceability.

Attachment: forensic_manifest_2027-05-03.pdf

- Rishi
Senior Forensics Engineer
Redwood Inference
